subject: knight
pitch: A fantasy knight in battle-worn plate armour. A great helm with a narrow eye slit and a tall crimson plume, layered shoulder plates etched with gold filigree, a deep-blue surcoat with a silver griffin emblem, a tall kite shield bearing the same griffin, and a broadsword. Dents and scratches tell of many battles, and a torn crimson cape hangs from the shoulders.
reasoning:
I'm wary of guessing exact SDK signatures wrong, so I want to stick to the safest subset of builder methods I'm confident about, favoring plain primitives over uncertain option formats.

Since I'm not sure whether joints return a bone or an object directly, I'll write a helper that resolves the joint to its underlying Object3D (checking for .bone or .object properties, falling back to root) and manually compute local mesh offsets from world positions I track myself, assuming rest-pose joints are unrotated. That should be reliable enough to start designing the knight at roughly human height.

Now I'm laying out the skeleton: hips, spine, chest, neck, head, leg chains, arm chains, with the sword on the right hand and shield on the left in a slight A-pose. I'm also setting up cached, flat-shaded standard materials with adjustable metalness, plus a cylinder-segment helper for building limbs between two joint points.

Writing leg geometry and surcoat skirt...

Skipping canvas textures due to environment risk, I'll build the griffin emblem from primitive geometry instead—a stylized silhouette using an extruded polygon shape that I can mirror and reuse for the shield and surcoat at different scales.

Still writing outline coordinates...

Still plotting griffin points...

I'm positioning the shield on the forearm with a tall blue field, silver border, and griffin emblem with darker dent details, then moving to the great helm design—a cylinder with a flat-top cone cap, dark eye slit, ridge straps, and a tall plume.

For the plume, I'm building a curved chain of crimson capsule segments arcing back from the crest using a Catmull-Rom curve, deciding to skip adding a jaw joint since the helm covers it. Then I'm layering the pauldrons with stacked spherical caps and gold trim rings.

Now I'm designing the arms with a shoulder-elbow-wrist chain in an A-pose, adding vambrace and gauntlet geometry, and positioning the right hand to grip a broadsword held point-up.

Sword construction next: grip, crossguard, pommel, and a tapered blade with a fuller line, sized heroically tall with a slight forward tilt. Then I'm planning the torn crimson cape as hanging strip panels attached behind the shoulders.

Adding ragged cape strips...

I'm adding a gold clasp chain, neck gorget, belt with buckle, and tassets, plus dents and scratches using randomized flattened spheres and thin boxes on the breastplate, shield, and helm. Now I'm setting up the floor alignment so sabatons rest at y=0 and starting the joint builder code with named joint positions.

Working out joint-to-object resolution logic, falling back to the root when a joint handle isn't directly an Object3D, and tracking world-space offsets so child objects position correctly relative to their parent joints...

Now I'm setting up a color palette (steel, gold, blue, crimson, silver, leather, dark tones) and a cached material helper, plus utility functions for adding meshes and building tapered cylinder segments between two points for limb/bone geometry.

For the pauldrons, I'm layering overlapping dome caps using partial sphere geometry, scaling and tilting them outward to create a stacked armor-plate look on each shoulder, mirrored across left and right sides.

I'm adding gold trim details—thin torus rings at the base of each layer and smaller studded rings along the dome's latitude lines, plus small gold spheres as decorative accents, grouping each layer so position and rotation apply together.

For the plume, I'm sampling points along a curved path to build tapered box segments oriented with quaternions along the tangent, adding smaller angled tufts on either side for volume, with a gold holder at the base. Now I'm shaping the helm itself with a tapered cylinder and conical dome top.

Still placing helm details...

Now I'm working out the torso geometry: a gorget cylinder at the neck, then a breastplate built from frustum shapes narrowing from chest to waist, with a surcoat panel positioned in front and back to sit over the armor while leaving shoulder gaps for the tabard.

For the tabard itself, I'm shaping a trapezoid with a pointed hem using an extruded polygon—defining front points that flare slightly wider at the bottom before tapering to a V shape, positioned to hang from the waist down to around the hip line.

I'm adding a small griffin emblem to the tabard front, sized around .38 tall and placed centered at chest height, finished in silver. I'll mirror a similar tabard panel on the back, plus a cape layer behind it, then move on to building the pelvis piece.

Now I'm fitting a leather belt over the tabard at the hip, sizing the cylinder radius so it sits just outside the tabard surface without clipping, with a gold buckle box placed at the front center.

For the shield, I'm positioning it in front of the left forearm, angling it outward with a slight y-rotation, then adjusting its height and x-offset so the top edge clears the shoulder pauldron instead of overlapping it.

Still writing shield geometry...

I'm attaching the shield to the elbow joint with an inset scale, adding worn details like scratches and dents, then moving on to sketch the hidden fist gauntlet and plan the cape strips hanging from the back with randomized lengths and backward tilt.

Writing cape geometry...

I'm also adding shoulder collar pieces with a gold chain clasp, then setting up a dent function to place battle damage marks across the helm, pauldrons, greaves, shield, and gauntlets, before starting the joint hierarchy for the hips and spine.

Defining the limb joint chain...

Defaulting the offset to zero when the joint equals root, otherwise using its position vector. Now I'm working out the sword geometry at the right wrist—grip, pommel, guard, and a tapered blade built from an extrusion shape.

Adding the fuller detail, gauntlet hand box, and a slight outward tilt rotation on the sword, then moving on to the sabaton boot dimensions anchored at the ankle.

Now I'm setting up a shape extrusion helper and planning the griffin construction with polygon and ellipse-based body parts, using semi-transparent materials for the figures.
